summary.prose: This Story lets a design document too long for one call be reviewed in coherent parts that still give one result. The document is split at its headings into whole sections. A section is kept with the sections it links to or whose ids it uses, and with its sibling sections, and each chunk gets the document's outline and a short summary of every related section held in another chunk. An HLD or LLD review then runs one reviewer session per chunk under today's checklist and merges the answers item by item, with extra checks that sections in different chunks agree. A DEF or plan review extracts its premises chunk by chunk and verifies them one by one as today. Under the limit, every review is exactly today's.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A new shared module, the review pipeline (proposed at src/workflow/review-pipeline), owns the three stages for every review. It is a serialisable job: the daemon drives it to the end; the controller is handed its calls one frame at a time and answers them by call identifier. Prepare measures material at 3 characters per token against review.chunkTokens (default 128,000 tokens); at or under the limit it emits one chunk whose prompt is the adapter's current single-call prompt, otherwise it groups the adapter's atoms by the adapter's relations and packs whole groups into chunks that each fit, adding a short summary of each related atom held in another chunk. Review issues one call per chunk serially; every call carries a fresh UUID that the answer must echo inside an envelope, an answer whose identifier is missing or wrong is rejected and retried under a new UUID, and a size refusal re-divides the chunk instead of resending it. Gather passes a single chunk's answer through unchanged and otherwise applies the adapter's gather rules (keyed obligations judged on all chunks' evidence, cross-chunk relationships, cross-chunk duplicates), each gather call itself bounded by the chunk limit. ISSUE-aef82b03's delivered InputTooLargeError, LLMProvider.inputBudgetChars, packIntoBatches and ReviewJob loop are moved under the pipeline as its core. A review kind is a series of stages, each a model stage or a deterministic one, preserving today's execution exactly: code review runs one stage per dimension exactly as today on each path: on the daemon, adherence (no call at all when there is neither an approved LLD nor an approved plan), conventions, coverage, quality and functional coverage are model calls, ux is deterministic and provider-free, and diagram keeps its registered handlers (some deterministic, such as the component handler) with today's per-handler isolation, a failing handler still recorded as a LOW observation; on the controller path the ux and diagram prompts are offered to the controller as today; HLD/LLD template review is one reviewer-session stage; DEF/plan premise review is extract (model), probe (deterministic) and verify, where the daemon path verifies one premise per call and the controller path verifies every premise in one batched call, as each does today; an adapter therefore declares its stage plan per path (daemon or controller). A review under the limit therefore makes exactly today's calls in today's order. Each call names its execution mode: a structured call run in the repository as its working directory (as today's code-review judges pass subject.repoPath; for the premise review's verify calls, which pass no working directory today, this is an additive change), each with its own per-call time limit where it has one today (the premise verify call keeps its 3-minute VERIFY_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS from ISSUE-d4b2cd1c), or a read-only reviewer session with the repository as working directory, the review's remaining deadline and its cancellation signal. Ollama gains a reviewer session through a generic read-only tool loop extracted from the analyzer's runShaperToolLoop, taking caller-supplied messages, answer schema, deadline, signal and retry policy, while the analyzer keeps its own wrapper unchanged. The pipeline owns every retry of a review call: every provider is called with internalRetry: false (CliProvider's transient retry and reviewer-session retry, and both providers' structured-output retry, make exactly one attempt), and the pipeline re-issues a transient failure, a stall, an invalid answer or an identifier mismatch once, under a new UUID: two attempts in all per call. Failure policy is per stage: a cancelled review always ends at once; a premise-review verify call that fails both attempts records that premise as not judged (MED, never a pass) and keeps the rest, as ISSUE-d4b2cd1c delivered; a diagram handler failure stays a LOW observation, as today; any other failed call (premise extraction included) fails the review and records nothing, as today. Gather is bounded at every step: an obligation's evidence (notes from every chunk, each keyed by the obligation and carrying the atom ids it stands for) is packed into the final adjudication call when it fits the limit; when it does not, it is reduced level by level, each reduction call reading one batch of that key's evidence and returning one note of at most a quarter of the limit under the same key, the job keeping which atoms and earlier notes each note stands for, until the key's evidence fits one adjudication call; a gather call refused for its size is re-planned like a chunk. Scope of the identifier and limit rules (stakeholder decision 2026-10-19 [[c14]]): they apply to every request the pipeline sends. A reviewer session's internal tool turns belong to the session, as they already do inside the claude and codex CLIs, where insrc cannot see them; the Ollama session's tool loop is likewise not identified or measured per turn. Every call records which material it carries (its chunk, atom ids and evidence-note ids), and the job keeps an immutable snapshot of the review's material taken once at prepare: for code review, today's grounding snapshot (the controller step already saves subject and grounding) plus every fact a deterministic stage reads from disk today, recorded at prepare (the ux stage's companion-mock existence checks); for design review, the document text and, for the premise review, the extracted claims and their gathered evidence. The adapter is rebuilt on every turn from the saved subject plus that snapshot and never re-queries the code graph or the files, so a refused call is re-divided from exactly the material it carried and a controller review resumes on the same material. A controller reports a call it could not complete as a failure outcome keyed by the call's identifier (size refusal with the reported limit, stall, transient error), which the driver handles exactly as a daemon-side failure: a size refusal re-divides the call, the others are re-issued once under a new identifier.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewMaterial
consumedContracts.purpose: What an adapter hands the pipeline to prepare: whole indivisible atoms, the relations between them, and the obligations a gather must judge.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewAdapter
consumedContracts.purpose: How a review kind plugs into the pipeline: its material, its ordered stages (model or deterministic) with each stage's own failure policy, each stage's calls for the whole review and for one chunk, and the gather rules for a divided review.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewChunk and ChunkPlan
consumedContracts.purpose: The output of prepare: the chunks a review is read in, each within the limit, with summaries of related atoms held elsewhere.

consumedContracts.name: CallEnvelope
consumedContracts.purpose: Every model call of every review carries a fresh identifier the answer must echo, and every retry is the pipeline's own re-issue under a new identifier; one rule for daemon and controller. The rule covers every request the pipeline sends; a reviewer session's internal tool turns are the session's own.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewPipelineJob
consumedContracts.purpose: The serialisable state of one review's pipeline run, driven to the end by the daemon or one frame at a time by the controller.

consumedContracts.name: Chunk limit setting
consumedContracts.purpose: One limit for every provider and every review kind.

boundary.internal: The design-review adapter: document sections as atoms, cross-reference relations, section summaries for neighbours, chunk prompts for the template checklist and the premise pipeline, and the gather of checklist answers or premise verdicts into today's ReviewReport and verdict rules. Tests: S004/ac1 every section appears whole in some chunk with the sections it references; ac2 a cross-chunk reference yields a section summary; ac3 a divided HLD/LLD review and a divided DEF/plan review each give one ReviewReport under today's verdict rules, and a premise whose call fails twice is still recorded as not judged. Its controller stage plan keeps today's single batched verify prompt under the limit; over the limit it batches premises per chunk.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The pipeline module itself: measurement, the generic grouping that packs related atoms together within the limit, staged execution with deterministic stages, the envelope schema wrapping, identifier generation and checking, the pipeline-owned retry policy (providers called with internalRetry: false; one re-issue under a new UUID, two attempts in all), per-stage failure policies, refusal re-division, the serial daemon driver, single-chunk pass-through, the bounded gather machinery (evidence notes keyed by obligation, level-by-level reduction under a note cap, provenance kept in the job, refused gather calls re-planned), and the adoption of ISSUE-aef82b03's InputTooLargeError, inputBudgetChars, packIntoBatches and ReviewJob loop. Change sites beyond the new module: CliProvider (internalRetry honoured by withTransientRetry, runReviewSession and its structured-output retry; a size refusal in the claude reviewer-session error envelope and the codex session classified as InputTooLargeError, as completeStructured already does), OllamaProvider (internalRetry: false maps completeStructured to one attempt; a read-only reviewer session over a generic tool loop extracted from runShaperToolLoop in src/analyze/context/driver.ts, the analyzer keeping its own wrapper), and the single-chunk adapters for both review kinds, so every review takes the pipeline path from s1 on with today's calls and working directory (structured calls run in the repository, as today for code review; the premise review's verify calls gain it as an additive change): one model stage per model-judged code-review dimension, adherence making no call without an approved LLD or plan, ux deterministic on the daemon and diagram's handlers as today (deterministic ones stay deterministic, a failing handler stays a LOW observation); one reviewer session for HLD/LLD; extract, probe, then one verify per premise for DEF/plan, with ISSUE-d4b2cd1c's not-judged recording kept. Tests: S001/ac1 an under-limit code review, template review and premise review each make today's calls and give today's result (recorded fixtures), the diagram dimension included; ac2 a missing or wrong identifier is retried once under a new UUID and no prompt hash repeats, including transient errors, stalls and invalid answers on both CliProvider and OllamaProvider; premise extraction failing fails the review while a verify call failing twice records the premise as not judged; ac3 the default limit is 384,000 characters for every provider; ac4 a size refusal from completeStructured, the claude session envelope and the codex session re-divides the call and never resends it; ac5 a review on an Ollama provider completes through both execution modes; plus a live probe of the envelope schema on claude and codex. Also tested: an obligation whose evidence exceeds the limit is reduced level by level, every gather call fits, and the final verdict keeps every atom's provenance; every structured review call runs in the repository working directory. Also tested: a premise verify call keeps its 3-minute limit through the pipeline; a refused call is re-divided from exactly the atoms and notes it carried; the controller premise review under the limit still sends one batched verify prompt. Also tested: refusal re-planning reads only the job's material snapshot, never the graph or files, so a reindex between turns cannot change the material a call is re-divided from. The ux stage reads companion-mock existence from the snapshot's file facts recorded at prepare, not from disk; tested: adding or removing a mock after prepare does not change the review result.

The code-review adapter's material: changed-symbol atoms, call relations from the grounding's callers and callees among changed symbols, file and module relations, and how neighbour summaries are written for a changed symbol held in another chunk. Tests: S002/ac1 related changed symbols land in the same chunk before file and module grouping; ac2 a call relation cut between chunks yields a neighbour summary on both sides; ac3 every changed symbol appears whole in some chunk and one over the limit is named, never cut.

The code-review adapter's gather: per-dimension chunk prompts, obligation keys and their adjudication over all chunks' evidence, the cross-chunk relationship check, the cross-chunk duplicate comparison for quality, and the fold into today's DimensionResult and verdict. It also owns the acceptance smoke: Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s1's code review runs on the installed daemon, completes and records a verdict, with the chunk plan and calls per stage written to the smoke record. Tests: S003/ac1 a divided review and the same material reviewed in one call under a raised limit give the same obligation verdicts on fixtures that fit both ways; ac2 a mismatch between related functions in different chunks is reported; ac3 a cross-chunk duplicate is reported; ac4 the installed-daemon smoke above.

The two controller steps' use of the job, and the MCP boundary that admits it: the new answers phase in the insrc_review_step and insrc_code_review_step input schemas in src/mcp/server.ts, their registered schema contracts and tool descriptions, with schema and surface tests (src/mcp/__tests__/schema-registry.test.ts); keeping it in step state, frame sizing, answer validation by call identifier, and offering a review under the limit today's prompts as identified calls in the same frame shape. Compatibility: the controller step states gain an optional pipeline field; a state without it (saved before the change) is resumed on today's path; both stores are memory-only, so, as today, a state does not survive a daemon restart. Tests: S005/ac1 a controller review over the limit is handed the daemon's chunks one frame at a time and records the same kind of result; ac2 a missing or wrong identifier in an answer is rejected and the call offered again under a new UUID; ac3 a new controller review under the limit is offered today's prompts, each as an identified call, and gives today's result; a pre-change state resumes on today's emit_judgements / judgements (code review), emit_claims / claims and emit_verdicts / verdicts (DEF/plan premise review) and emit_findings / findings (HLD/LLD template review) frames, each path tested. The answers phase also accepts a failure outcome per call (size refusal with the reported limit, stall, transient error), mapped to the driver's failure handling and admitted by both MCP input schemas; tested: a controller-reported size refusal re-divides the call, a reported stall or transient error re-issues it once under a new identifier.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — divided code review and divided design review

nonFunctional.performance: Calls are serial (k6). A review under the limit makes the same number of calls as today. Every prompt sent, chunk or gather, is at most review.chunkTokens x 3 characters.
nonFunctional.security: No new transport: calls go through the existing LLMProvider and the installed CLIs (k7). Reviewer sessions keep their read-only tool sets.
nonFunctional.observability: Each review logs its plan (single or N chunks, chars per chunk), every call's identifier, stage and size, every identifier mismatch and refusal, and the gather's obligation count; DimensionResult and ReviewReport record the number of calls per stage when a review was divided.
nonFunctional.durability: The job is serialisable, so the controller path survives across turns in the existing step state (memory-only, so not across a daemon restart, as today). A daemon review whose call fails after its retries records nothing, as today, except the premise review, which records that premise as not judged and keeps the rest (ISSUE-d4b2cd1c). New record fields (pipelineCalls) are optional, under a new name, and absent on one-chunk reviews; the existing parts field keeps its shape; so existing records keep validating.

api.name: ReviewAdapter.material (design review)
api.signature: material(): ReviewMaterial  // built by designReviewMaterial(documentText: string, fits: (atomText: string) => boolean): ReviewMaterial

parameters.name: documentText
parameters.purpose: The document markdown in the job's snapshot (snapshot.documentText); never re-read from disk.

parameters.name: fits
parameters.purpose: Supplied by the adapter for its review kind: renders the minimal real call holding just this atom (the template session prompt with the resolved template and stage, or the extract prompt for the stage, plus the outline, title and envelope) and measures it against limitChars. designReviewMaterial stays a pure text parser and asks fits() only to decide subdivision.

returns.meaning: atoms: one per level-2 section (heading line plus body up to the next level-2 heading), in document order. A level-2 section for which fits() is false is replaced by its level-3 subsections (then level 4), each atom labelled with its heading path. The text between a parent heading and its first child heading travels with the first child. id = `sec<n>`, the section's occurrence index in document order (unique even when two sections share a heading), label = the heading path. The heading's anchor slug is kept separately and used only to resolve #anchor links; where two headings share a slug, the slug resolves the way markdown renderers do (the second gets the -1 suffix). The text before the first level-2 heading (title, metadata, summary and any body) is itself a reviewed atom, 'preamble', placed in the first chunk, so its premises are judged like any section's. A document with no level-2 heading is one atom: the whole document; if it does not fit, it is split at level-3 headings, and with none it is reported by AtomTooLargeError as 'the whole document (no headings)'. context: an 'outline' atom (every heading with its number) and the document's title line, carried by every chunk. relations: 'references' from a section to each section it links (#anchor links), cites by number (§2.4, section 2.4), or uses an id defined there (sc3, s2, k5, ac1, c14, t3, a1 and the like, resolved to the first section that defines the id as a heading, table row or list item); 'same-module' between sections under the same parent heading. obligations: ALWAYS empty, for both design adapters: s1 makes no obligation calls for a design review. The checklist is resolved once at prepare (resolveDesignReview, then reviewTemplateFor, as today), and the WHOLE resolved template ({ id, intent, maxPremises, items[{ id, dimension, check }] }) is saved with the job's subject, together with the review kind and stage. A rebuilt adapter uses that saved template and never re-reads the artifact store or readDesignReviewSettings, so a configuration change mid-review cannot alter it. The template's check items are never ReviewMaterial obligations: they are the checklist each chunk session answers, merged per item by the template adapter's merge.

errors.condition: A section with no smaller subsections for which fits() is false; named by its heading path.

preconditions: Built from the snapshot's document text only.
postconditions: Every character of the document belongs to exactly one reviewed atom; nothing is context-only.
Deterministic: the same text gives the same atoms, relations and order.

api.name: ReviewAdapter.neighbourSummary (design review)

parameters.name: atom
parameters.purpose: A related section held in another chunk.

parameters.name: material
parameters.purpose: To list the ids the section defines.

returns.meaning: The heading path, the ids the section defines, and its first sentences up to 300 characters, with no model call.

postconditions: The section itself is reviewed whole in its own chunk; only this extra line is shortened.

api.name: AdapterStage.chunkCalls (template review: one reviewer session per chunk)
api.signature: chunkCalls(chunk: ReviewChunk, prior: StageOutputs): readonly ChunkPrompt[]  // execution: { mode: 'reviewer-session', cwd: repo, deadlineMs, tools: 'read-only' }

parameters.name: chunk
parameters.purpose: The chunk's sections and neighbour summaries.

returns.meaning: One reviewer session per chunk: today's buildTemplateReviewPrompt system text (src/workflow/review/template.ts:182) and checklist, preceded by a note that this is part k of n of the document. The DESIGN part carries the preamble, the outline, the chunk's sections whole, and a 'related sections held in other parts' block of neighbour summaries. The reviewer judges premises found in these sections and answers every check item, using notApplicable for an item with nothing in these sections. The schema is today's TEMPLATE_ANSWER_SCHEMA.

preconditions: Used only when the plan is not single; under the limit the stage keeps today's single prompt.
postconditions: Each chunk answer passes validateTemplateAnswer (src/workflow/review/template.ts:310), with maxPremises as a ceiling per session.

api.name: AdapterStage.validate (template chunk answers)
api.signature: validate(answer: unknown, call: ReviewCall): readonly string[]

returns.meaning: The errors from validating a chunk answer with today's rules (the same checks validateTemplateAnswer makes). An invalid answer is re-issued once by the pipeline with today's correction text. A valid answer is kept as a ValidatedChunkAnswer, not converted to findings: { items: [{ item, notApplicable?: string, premises: [{ premise, outcome, severity, evidence, action, files: string[] }] }] }, produced by a new parseTemplateAnswer in src/workflow/review/template.ts. validateTemplateAnswer keeps its signature and result, implemented over the same parse.

api.name: AdapterStage.chunkCalls (premise review extract stage)
api.signature: chunkCalls(chunk: ReviewChunk, prior: StageOutputs): readonly ChunkPrompt[]  // execution: { mode: 'structured', cwd: repo }

parameters.name: chunk
parameters.purpose: The chunk's sections and neighbour summaries.

returns.meaning: One extract call per chunk: today's buildExtractPrompt (src/workflow/review/extract.ts:136) system text and EXTRACT_SCHEMA, over the outline and title, the chunk's sections and neighbour summaries, extracting the premises of these sections only. Chunk answers accumulate in the job's answered list, NOT in the snapshot. When the stage's last chunk answer has been applied, the stage output is written ONCE to snapshot.claims (s1's rule): every chunk's claims in chunk order, each re-keyed to a job-unique raw id `r<chunk>-<k>`, where k is the claim's position in that chunk's answer. The model's own id is kept separately as localId, because it can repeat within a chunk and across chunks. The deterministic probe stage (runStage) merges raw claims with the same normalised text and anchors into a MergedClaim: { id: `p<n>` numbered in first-appearance order, text, kind, anchors (union), probe (union of greps and reads, de-duplicated), sources: [{ rawId, localId, chunkId, ref? }], owningChunk: the first source's chunkId }. It gathers evidence for each merged claim, keyed by the merged id as Evidence is today, and outputs [{ claim, evidence }], which s1 writes once to snapshot.evidence. Verify, the controller's per-chunk batches (grouped by owningChunk) and any resumed or re-planned job read the merged claims from snapshot.evidence, never the raw snapshot.claims. MergedClaim is a Claim (same fields, id unique) plus sources and owningChunk, so verifyClaim, normalizeFinding and the id-keyed maps in runReview and handleVerdicts work unchanged.

postconditions: Premise extraction failing in any chunk after two attempts fails the review, as today (fail-review).

api.name: GatherPlan.relationCall (design review)

parameters.name: pair
parameters.purpose: A 'references' relation cut between chunks: the referring section and the referenced one.

returns.meaning: Template review only. For a cut 'references' relation, the call carries the FACTS on both sides, quoted whole and never shortened. From the referenced section: the definition excerpt of each id, anchor or number the referring section uses (the heading block, table row, list item or paragraph that defines it). From the referring section: every paragraph, row or list item that mentions it. Facts beyond either section's opening are therefore always compared. When all of a pair's excerpts do not fit one call, they are split per referenced id. For each id, its usage excerpts are packed by the s1 packer into batches that each fit WITH that id's definition excerpt, giving one call per batch, so every returned call fits limitChars. If the definition excerpt and a single usage excerpt cannot fit together, AtomTooLargeError names the pair (the id, the defining heading and the using heading); a single excerpt larger than the limit is named the same way. Each call records its provenance: the two section ids, the referenced id, and the excerpts it carries. Each call asks whether the uses agree with the definition (names, signatures, ids, numbers, rules) and returns premises in today's template premise shape, each under a check item id of the template. A premise review makes no relation calls.

postconditions: Each cut reference is checked on its full definition and every usage excerpt, across as many calls as needed.
The provenance of each relation premise is kept in the job.

api.name: GatherPlan.merge / ReviewAdapter.finish (design review)
api.signature: template adapter, R = ValidatedChunkAnswer: merge(parts: readonly ValidatedChunkAnswer[]): ValidatedChunkAnswer; finish(outputs: StageOutputs): ValidatedChunkAnswer. premise adapter, R = readonly Finding[]: merge and finish over findings

parameters.name: parts

returns.type: R (ValidatedChunkAnswer for the template adapter; readonly Finding[] for the premise adapter)
returns.meaning: This satisfies sc2 as written: merge(parts: R[]) => R and finish => R, each with one R per adapter. Template adapter: merge per check item as before (premises unioned; identical premises, by normalised text and normalised file set, kept once with does-not-hold over could-not-verify over holds and HIGH over MED over LOW; notApplicable only when unanimous). It has no obligations, so s1 never calls its obligationCall or reduceCall (which return the empty-gather prompts) and makes no obligation calls. runTemplateReview takes the job's R and builds today's ReviewReport from it: it converts to findings exactly as validateTemplateAnswer does, assigns report-wide unique claimIds (`${item}.${n}` across each item's merged premises, relation premises included), and runs computeVerdict with today's blockOn, tally and the template id, setting pipelineCalls when divided. Premise adapter: R is the findings of every verified or not-judged premise; runReview folds them as today. The merged premise count may exceed maxPremises, which stays a per-session ceiling.

postconditions: Satisfies sc2's merge(parts: R[]) => R and finish => R.

errorCases.scenario: A section with no subsections is too large for any call.
errorCases.detection: designReviewMaterial measures the section's minimal call (instructions, preamble, outline, the section alone, the envelope) against limitChars after splitting down to its leaf headings.
errorCases.response: AtomTooLargeError naming the heading path, before any provider call. The section is never cut.
errorCases.userImpact: The review stops and names the section, rather than judging part of it.

errorCases.scenario: A chunk's template answer breaks the checklist (an item missing or doubled, too many premises, a does-not-hold premise without files).
errorCases.detection: AdapterStage.validate runs validateTemplateAnswer on the chunk answer.
errorCases.response: Re-issued once under a new callId with today's correction text, then fail-review: no review is recorded, as today.

errorCases.scenario: A relation answer names a check item id the template does not have.
errorCases.detection: validate(answer, call) checks every premise's item against the template's item ids.
errorCases.response: Invalid answer: one re-issue, then fail-review.
errorCases.userImpact: No premise is filed under an invented item.

errorCases.scenario: Extraction fails twice in one chunk of a premise review.
errorCases.detection: The extract stage's onCallFailure is fail-review.
errorCases.response: The review fails and records nothing, as today.

errorCases.scenario: A premise's verify call fails twice in a divided review.
errorCases.detection: The verify stage's onCallFailure is record-not-judged.
errorCases.response: That premise is recorded as a MED not-judged finding; the rest are kept (ISSUE-d4b2cd1c).
errorCases.userImpact: The review blocks under the default policy, but is recorded.

errorCases.scenario: The divided template review runs past its time limit.
errorCases.detection: s1's driver compares now with job.deadlineAt before each session, and each session runs with the remaining time.
errorCases.response: The review fails with today's time-limit message and records nothing.
errorCases.userImpact: Rare: the budget is the per-session limit times the planned sessions (s1's amended rule), so only sessions that each run near their limit exhaust it.

errorCases.scenario: Two chunks produce findings for the same check item.
errorCases.detection: finish numbers claimIds across the merged premises of each item.
errorCases.response: Every finding gets a unique claimId, so a resolution recorded against one never applies to another.
errorCases.userImpact: Resolving one finding leaves the others blocking as they should.

alternativesConsidered.name: Sections as atoms with reference relations; per-chunk sessions and extraction; deterministic merge plus relation checks
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A design-review material builder turns the snapshot's document text into heading-section atoms with 'references' and 'same-module' relations and a deterministic outline context. Divided template reviews run one reviewer session per chunk and merge the checklist answers per item, with relation calls checking cut references. Divided premise reviews extract claims per chunk, de-duplicate them, and verify as today.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Material: the document is split at level-2 headings. A level-2 section larger than the limit is split into its level-3 subsections (then level 4), each atom keeping its heading path, and a leaf section still too large raises s1's AtomTooLargeError naming its heading. The text before the first level-2 heading is itself a reviewed atom ('preamble', in the first chunk), and a generated outline of every heading plus the title line is context carried by every chunk; a heading-free document is one atom. Relations: 'references' from a section to each section it links (#anchor links, numbered references such as §2.4, and ids such as sc3, s2, k5, ac1 or c14, resolved to the section that defines them); 'same-module' between sections under the same parent heading. neighbourSummary writes the heading path, the ids the section defines and its first sentences up to 300 characters, with no model call. Template review over the limit: one reviewer-session call per chunk with today's checklist rules, the outline and preamble, the chunk's sections and their neighbour summaries. The reviewer judges the premises of these sections and answers every check item (premises, or notApplicable meaning 'nothing in these sections'). Each chunk answer is validated by validateTemplateAnswer, with maxPremises as a per-session ceiling. Gather merges per check item: the union of premises, with identical premises (same normalised text and files) kept once at their worst outcome; an item is notApplicable only if every chunk says so. relationCall checks each cut 'references' relation on the full definition excerpts of the referenced ids and every usage excerpt in the referring section (batched per id so each call fits), reporting a premise under the check item it names (validated against the template's ids) when the two sections disagree. Premise review over the limit: the extract stage runs per chunk with the outline and neighbour summaries; claims from all chunks are de-duplicated (same normalised text and anchors) and given ids in chunk order before they enter the snapshot; probe and verify run per claim as today, since a verify prompt holds the claim and evidence, not the document. Controller path: one batched verify prompt per chunk's claims over the limit, today's single batch under it. finish merges validated chunk answers per item, assigns report-wide unique claimIds, and folds the findings with computeVerdict and today's blockOn, tally and the template id; pipelineCalls is set when divided.
pros: Every section is reviewed whole, with the sections it references or their summaries.
Reuses today's checklist, validator, verify and verdict code unchanged; only the chunk prompts and the merge are new.
Cross-chunk consistency is checked explicitly by relation calls.
The premise path changes only extraction; verification stays per claim.
cons: A divided template review runs several reviewer sessions, so the review's time budget must cover them. s1 caps a review's limit at 30 minutes (HARD_REVIEW_DEADLINE_MS), so a long document can run out of time. Settling the budget is s1's deadline rule, raised as an open question.
Reference resolution relies on recognisable links and ids; a reference written in plain prose is not seen, though same-module relations keep sibling sections together.

constraintScore.notes: Heading sections are whole atoms, grouped by references and parent heading; an oversized leaf is named.
neighbourSummary for each referenced section held elsewhere.
Per-item merge and per-claim verify fold through computeVerdict and today's blockOn.
Claims are de-duplicated before entering the snapshot.
Complete only if the review's time budget covers every session (open question on s1's deadline).

alternativesConsidered.name: One reviewer session that reads the document from disk
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: For template reviews, send the outline and the document path instead of its text and let one reviewer session read the sections it needs; premise reviews divide extraction as in a1.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The reviewer session already has read-only tools, so the prompt carries the checklist, the outline and the path, and the session reads sections itself. The session's own context management handles size. Premise extraction is divided as in a1.
pros: One session and one deadline, as today; no merge for template reviews.
cons: Nothing ensures every section is read: the reviewer may skip sections, which breaks ac1 and k5.
The session's internal reads are not measured, so it can still overflow its own context, with no division to fall back on.
Departs from the HLD's prepare, review and gather for design review.

constraintScore.notes: No guarantee every section is reviewed.
No chunk plan for template reviews.

alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Simple, but cannot guarantee every section is read, and the session can still overflow.

alternativesConsidered.name: Sequential section packing without references
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Sections are packed in document order until a chunk is full; no relations, no neighbour summaries, no relation checks.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Atoms as in a1, but chunks are consecutive sections packed by size, and gather is the per-item union only.
cons: A section can land apart from the sections it references with no summary of them, which fails ac1 and ac2.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Divides by size alone, which the Epic rules out.
